ctx.x: So then, again, I was in Washington without a job, and so it meant I started working in clubs, in one thing or another. I think during that time, any time I had a job almost it was one I organized and got myself, by having a trio or a band or some kind of.... It's kind of funny. If you get into a situation like that, where you are a bandleader for any length of time, it seems as if the only time you ever get a job or anybody ever calls you for a job is... As a matter of fact, no one ever calls you. Any job that…

Anyway, late in 1954, I got this call from Al Hibbler in New York, telling me that he had just recorded an album, and he was going out on his own, and he would like for me to travel with him as his pianist. And I'd known Al from a long time back, from the days in Chicago, the Trummy Young days. We had been friends through the years and everything. So it was always a pleasure to work with Al.
